title: The Effects of Expectations on Emotional Processing
summary:
The aim of this study is to examine whether emotional expectations influence the perception of emotional facial expressions. It will also be investigated whether such effects are reflected in brain activity and facial muscle responses.
Emotional expectations will be created using a simulated Brain-Computer Interface, which presents colored visual cues suggesting a positive (green) or negative (red) emotional brain state. A yellow cue will indicate that no feedback is provided and serves as a control condition. 
These cues are not based on actual brain activity but are intended to influence participants’ expectations. After each cue and a short anticipation phase, participants will view facial expressions that vary in emotional intensity and rate their perceived valence.

interventions.name:
All three conditions (corresponding to Arm 1, Arm 2, and Arm 3) are presented to each participant in a pseudorandomized order.

Arm 2 – Nocebo condition: 
A red visual cue, framed as the output of a sham Brain-Computer Interface (BCI), is used to induce the expectation of a negative emotional brain state.

Arm 3 –Control condition: 
A yellow visual cue signals the absence of BCI feedback, functioning as the control condition without directed expectation induction.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy
Exclusion criteria:
Contraindications for EEG (e.g., scalp conditions)
Red-green colour blindness
Presence of acute or chronic somatic or psychiatric disorders
Pregnancy
Regular use of medication (except hormonal contraceptives)
Use of illegal drugs
Participation in a study involving deception within the past six months
